governed_construct: A class: every ClassDeclaration or ClassExpression in the file (including abstract classes and React class components). Interfaces, type aliases, object literals and functions are not classes and are not instances.
interpretation: Each class is one instance and conforms only if all three measurable limits hold: (1) fewer than 10 public methods, (2) fewer than 10 properties, (3) fewer than 200 instructions. 'Single purpose' is not mechanically checkable and is not used for the verdict. Public methods = method declarations and get/set accessors in the class body (static or instance, sync or async) that are not marked private or protected and do not have a #private name; the constructor is not counted; arrow functions assigned to fields are properties, not methods. Properties = all property declarations in the class body regardless of accessibility (public, private, protected, readonly, static, #private, with or without initializer), plus TypeScript constructor parameter properties (parameters carrying public/private/protected/readonly), plus distinct names assigned as `this.name = ...` in the constructor body that are not already declared (the JavaScript idiom for declaring fields). Instructions = statement nodes nested anywhere inside the class's members, counted recursively; a class with 200 or more is VIOLATED. Exactly 10 public methods or exactly 10 properties is VIOLATED ('less than 10'). A file is VIOLATED if any class breaks any limit, SATISFIED if it has at least one class and all conform, NOT_APPLICABLE if it contains no class. Object literals with many methods and interfaces with many members are not classes and are ignored.
